• Calcium oxide (CaO)__, commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.

 
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid at room temperature.

• **IUPAC ID**: Oxocalcium
 
• **Molar mass**: 56.0774 g/mol
 
• **Melting point**: 2,572 °C
 
• **Density**: 3.34 g/cm³​
 
• **Soluble in:** Water, Glycerol.
 
 

***Thus I is incorrect.***

 
• Aluminium oxide is a white odourless crystalline powder. It is water-insoluble.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide contains approximately ______ of oxygen for each 1.00 g of carbon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.33 g.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Every sample of **carbon monoxide contains 16.0 g of oxygen** for** every 12.0 g of carbon.**
 
• **This is a mass ratio of oxygen to carbon of 1.33 to 1.**
 
• In carbon dioxide, there is exactly twice as much oxygen present as there is in carbon monoxide.
 
• This** illustrates the law of multiple proportions:**
 
 
• whenever the same two elements form more than one compound, the different masses of one element that combine with the same mass of the other element are in the ratio of small whole numbers.
 
 
 
• **In carbon monoxide, there is ****1.333g ****oxygen for every ****1g ****carbon.**
 
• In carbon dioxide, there is 2.666g oxygen for every gram of carbon.
 
• So** the ratio of oxygen in the two compounds is 1:2, a small whole-number ratio.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon monoxide is a deadly gas. **
 
• It is formed from the incomplete combustion of some carbon-containing materials (such as wood and gasoline).
 
• It will attach to haemoglobin in the red blood cells and block the binding of oxygen to those cells.
 
• If oxygen does not bind, it cannot be carried to the cells of the body where it is needed, and** death can occur**.
 
• **Carbon dioxide, on the other hand, is not toxic like carbon monoxide is. **
 
• However, it can displace oxygen in systems since it is heavier.
 
• **Carbon dioxide fire extinguishers cut off the flow of oxygen in a fire, putting out the fire.**

• It is used as an** important reagent in lanthanide **chemistry.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristics of amorphous solids?

options.text: A definite and characteristic enthalpy of fusion
Melting at a sharp and characteristic temperature
Gradual softening over a range of temperatures

questions.solution:
**Explanation:-**

**Amorphous Solid:-**

 
• There is a lack of long-term planning.
 
• The constituent particles of an amorphous solid do not have a long-range order of arrangement.
 
• There is no distinct melting point. Amorphous solids do not have a distinct melting point and melt at a variety of temperatures.
 
• Conversion from a liquid to a crystalline state.
 
• Amorphous solids have two distinct characteristics.
 
• When cleaved or split, they form pieces with irregular, typically curved surfaces, and when exposed to x-rays, their components are not ordered in a regular array, resulting in poorly defined patterns.
 
• Glass is an amorphous, translucent substance.
 
• Amorphous solids are solids that lack a distinct geometry, have identical characteristics along all axes, melt across a wide range, and shatter into curved or irregular shapes.
 
• It's vital to remember that these phrases represent two opposite ends of a spectrum.
 
• Short-range order exists in most amorphous substances.

questions.question: What is the valency of Boron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **number of atoms** of one element coupled with **one atom of another** to create a **molecule** is known as **valency.**
 
• **Valency and molecular weight** are two related terms.
 
• The** quantity of electrons **in an** element's outermost shell **determines its valency.
 
• **Valence electrons **are the electrons that make up the** outermost shell surrounding an atomic nucleus.**
 
• The **nucleus **of an atom is composed of **protons and neutrons. **
 
• **Electrons **revolve around the nucleus in a fixed path called **orbits or shells.**
 
• The names of the shells are** "K," "L," "M," "N," **and so forth.
 
• The **'K' shel**l, which may hold up to **2 electrons**, is the innermost shell.
 
• The **"L" shell**, which has up to **8 electrons**, comes next.
 
• The** "M" shell, **which has up to **18 electrons**, comes next.
 
• Up to** 32 electrons** can be found in the last **"N" shell.**​
 
• **Boron:**
 
 
• The atomic number of boron is **5.**
 
• There are** fewer than five electrons—three**—in the outer shell.
 
• It needs to provide or release these **electrons to stay stable.**
 
• **Two electrons **are located in the** K shell **and three are located in the** L shell **in accordance with the** octet rule.**
 
• It'll lose **three electrons.**
 
• The result is that boron has a **valency of 3.**​

questions.question: What is the ratio by mass of nitrogen and hydrogen in ammonia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 **____**∶ 3**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Ammonia (NH3)**

__
 
• The law of constant composition states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio (by mass) and does not depend on its source and method of preparation.
 
• Nitrogen makes up about 14/17 of the mass of any sample of pure Ammonia, while Hydrogen makes up the remaining 3/17 of the mass. (Atomic weight of nitrogen is 14 and that of hydrogen is 1)
 
• That is Ammonia, **Nitrogen, and Hydrogen are always present in the ratio 14:3 by mass.**
 
• 1 atom of Nitrogen is always combined with 3 atoms of Hydrogen.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Atomic mass is the quantity of matter contained in an atom of an element. 
 
• It is expressed as a multiple of one-twelfth the mass of the carbon-12 atom.
 
• Mass ratio, often called "per cent composition by mass," is the proportion of a particular molecule that consists of each of that molecule's constituent elements.
